headline: Gray Gems And Ninth Inning Explosion Fuel Massive Sox Win In Cleveland
morning_brew: Finally, the bats showed some signs of life in Cleveland. After a rough couple of games, we absolute steamrolled the Guardians in a nine to one victory on Saturday. Sonny Gray was outstanding on the mound, giving us six strong innings and allowing only one run while striking out seven. Connor Wong and Jarren Duran did the heavy lifting, driving in three runs apiece to fuel the offense. We broke the game wide open with a massive six-run explosion in the ninth inning, racking up eleven hits on the night. It is only one win, but seeing this lineup actually deliver in the clutch on the road is a sight for sore eyes.

Let's not get too carried away, though, because this team is still sitting at twenty-four and thirty-three, dead last in the AL East. We have the series decider this afternoon in Cleveland before heading back home to Fenway Park for a tough stretch against Baltimore. If we want any chance of digging ourselves out of this basement, we need to build some actual momentum instead of following up every great win with a three-game slide. The bullpen actually held their ground on Saturday, with Tyron Guerrero, Justin Slaten, and Danny Coulombe keeping the door shut, which is exactly what we need to see on a consistent basis.

With both the Celtics and Bruins in the offseason, the rumor mill is starting to heat up around the Hub. The NBA approved some new draft lottery reforms to stop tanking, but honestly, that does not mean a whole lot for our guys who are just trying to rebuild after that brutal first-round exit. Over on the ice, the Bruins have some massive roster decisions to make before free agency opens on July first. Management has to find some scoring depth to help David Pastrnak, because standing pat this summer is simply not an option after watching the playoffs from home.
